rated_messages.input_message: Urges can feel like stormy weather. But if you're the sky, you just let that storm come and go on it's own knowing that it won't last forever.
If you have trouble resisting a craving when other smokers are around, try carrying a water bottle and taking a sip every time you want to ask for a cig.

To keep on track, small changes can really help. For example, keep a list of quit reasons where you used to keep cigarettes, rearrange your living space, or grab some extra pens to fiddle with to keep your hands busy.
Keep picturing yourself getting home later today knowing that you've gained a smoke-free day. It's nearly a reality!
What can you do right now to break the automatic habit of smoking to help you feel better? Pause. Close your eyes. And take 10 slow breaths.
No need to get rid of these feelings or control them with a smoke. They are not permanent.
Don't test yourself needlessly. If this social situation gets uncomfortable then leave briefly if you can. It really helps and it's fine to do it more than once!

Imagine that your urge is a backseat passenger trying to distract you from reaching your destination. See if you can choose to keep driving instead of allowing your urges to distract you from where you want to go.

Don't let anyone tell you how you should or shouldn't feel today. You feel how you feel and that's it. If you're happy and grateful then enjoy the moment, if you're angry and frustrated, know that this will pass.
Take a slow, deep breath in. And let it out. Now, ask yourself, "Am I willing to go one minute without smoking?" When that minute is over, ask yourself this question again.
